title: Merge Sorted Array
statement_short: Given two integer arrays sorted in non-decreasing order, merge the second array into the first array as a single sorted array in-place. The first array has additional empty space at the end to accommodate all elements.
hint: Small n and m do not restrict time complexity, but in-place merging requires O(1) extra space.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers iterating backward from the ends of both arrays merge elements in-place in O(m+n) time. Not Sorting: Concatenating and sorting takes O((m+n) log(m+n)) time. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Inserting all elements into a min-heap takes O((m+n) log(m+n)) time and extra space. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash tables do not preserve order and incur unnecessary space overhead.

title: Remove Element
statement_short: Given an integer array and a target value, remove all occurrences of that target value in-place. Return the number of elements remaining after placing valid elements in the front of the array.
hint: Small array size places no time restriction, but elements must be overwritten in-place with O(1) space.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers (read and write indices) overwrite target values in a single O(n) pass in-place. Not Sliding Window: The task requires modifying array elements across the entire array, not identifying an optimal continuous window. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Using a hash set requires O(n) auxiliary space, violating the in-place constraint. Not Stack: Pushing valid elements to a stack consumes O(n) extra memory.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement_short: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place so that each unique element appears only once while keeping their relative order. Return the count of unique elements.
hint: Input length up to 3 * 10^4 requires an O(n) time solution, while sorted order enables linear in-place tracking.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers exploit sorted order to overwrite adjacent duplicates in-place in O(n) time. Not HashMap / Hash Set: A hash set identifies unique items but uses unnecessary O(n) space. Not Binary Search: Binary search locates values in logarithmic time but cannot perform in-place array compaction. Not Monotonic Stack: Stack tracking is unnecessary because the input array is already sorted.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
statement_short: Given a sorted integer array, remove excess duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears at most twice while preserving relative order. Return the updated array length.
hint: Input size up to 3 * 10^4 requires O(n) time, and pre-sorted order permits fixed-offset duplicate checks.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers compare the reader element against writer-2 to allow at most two copies in-place in O(n) time. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming transitions are unnecessary for simple conditional array overwrite. Not Sliding Window: The problem asks for modifying sequence elements, not finding a max/min subsegment window. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Tracking element frequencies in a hash map uses O(n) auxiliary space.

title: Majority Element
statement_short: Given an array of size n, find the element that appears more than floor(n / 2) times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the input array.
hint: Input size up to 5 * 10^4 requires O(n) time, and the guaranteed majority property enables O(1) space element cancellation.
why_not: Right: Boyer-Moore Voting pairs majority and minority items to cancel non-majority elements in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Sorting: Sorting puts the majority element at index n/2 but costs O(n log n) time. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Frequency counting takes O(n) time but requires O(n) extra space. Not Bit Manipulation: Bitwise counting takes O(32n) time, which is slower than linear voting.
